entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ravindra Kumar Yadav
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the informant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material brought on record.

2. The present bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in case crime No. 163/2020,
under Section 506, 376 IPC & Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, police station Saraimeer, District Azamgarh with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
3. It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant-accused is innocent and he has not committed any offence.
As per ossification test report, age of victim has been found between 16 to 18 years and thus, she is a major girl.

It was submitted that in her statement, recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., victim has stated that applicant has established physical relations with Ubaida vs State Of U.P. on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16321360/
1 her with consent but when she became pregnant, he has refused to marry with her.
Both the parties belong to Mahomedan religion and applicant is ready to marry with victim and to accept the child of victim.
Learned counsel submitted that in case applicant is released on bail, he would accept the child of victim and would marry with victim.
Referring to statement of victim and facts of the matter, it was submitted that relations between victim and applicant were consensual in nature.
It is further submitted that statements of all the material witnesses, including victim, have already been recorded before the trial court and there is no possibility of tampering with the evidence.

Learned counsel has also referred the case of Mrigraj Gautam @ Rippu, [Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.
45007 of 2023], decided on 26.10.2023.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
Lastly, it was submitted that the applicant is in judicial custody since 03.09.2020, having no criminal history, and that in case applicant is enlarged on bail,
the applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail.

4. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have opposed the prayer for bail and argued that as per DNA report, applicant has been found biological father of the child of victim and that victim has made allegations of rape against the applicant.

5. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of custody and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits, a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

6. Let the applicant Ubaida involved in the aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two local sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of court concerned subject to the following conditions:
i.
The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during trial.
ii. The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
iii. The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant will not try to contact, threat or otherwise influence the complainant or any of the witness of the case.

7. In case of breach of any of the above conditions or breach of promise about marriage and acceptance of child, the informant/prosecution shall be at liberty to move an application for cancellation of bail of the applicant and the court concerned would be at liberty to cancel the bail of applicant, in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 15.3.2024 Anand  Ubaida vs State Of U.P. on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16321360/
